question: A theme park's annual figure is 9 times the energy booked to one ride, and each ride dispatches 8 identical cars in a cycle. For one car the booked energy is its kinetic energy plus 9 J charged to the lap-bar release, expressed in kilojoules. A loaded car has a mass of 48 kg, and the station platform is 12 m long. The car's speed at the bottom of the drop, in metres per second, is the larger of the two values whose square, minus 4 times the value, plus 3, comes to exactly 0. What is the theme park's annual figure, in kJ?

A pile-driving rig logs its hammer's acceleration, in metres per second squared, as the total accumulated between the 2nd and the 3rd second of a stroke, where the instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 2 times t squared plus 4 times t. The hammer has a mass of 135000 g. The rig's guide mast stands 18 m tall. Eight identical hammers fall together on one frame, so the frame carries 8 times the force of a single hammer, and the contractor operates 5 such frames at once. What total force do the 5 frames carry, in kN?

A robotics lab reports 9 times a single arm's corrected thrust, because nine arms work the same cell. The corrected thrust for one arm is the force on its payload, plus 2 N for the gripper spring and a further 26 N for the wrist damper. The payload has a mass of 12000 g. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is 2 more than a number x, where x is the smaller of the two values satisfying x squared minus 7 times x plus 10 equals 0. What does the lab report, in N?

A quarry's shaker deck drives a screen assembly of mass 153000 g. The deck's drive is set so that the assembly's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is 6 times a number x, where x is the smaller of the two values for which x squared, minus 9 times x, plus 14, equals exactly 0. Eight identical decks are bolted to the same steel frame and all run in phase, so the frame takes 8 times the force of one deck. The maintenance log then subtracts 1 N to account for the calibration offset of the load pin. What figure goes in the maintenance log, in N?

A rail workshop's test summary is the energy carried by a runaway trolley, expressed in kilojoules, plus 7 kJ charged to the brake heater. The trolley has a mass of 41 kg. It runs at a speed, in metres per second, equal to twice a certain count. That count is the number of different pairs of tie-down points that can be chosen from the 9 tie-down points welded to the trolley floor, taking 2 at a time. What is the test summary figure, in kJ?

A cable test bench tracks a shuttle whose position along the guide, in metres, is 2 times the cube of the elapsed seconds minus 3 times the square of the elapsed seconds. The bench reads how fast the shuttle is moving at the instant 3 seconds in, subtracts 26 from that reading, and multiplies the remainder by 4 to obtain the launch speed, in metres per second, used for the next stage. The launched body has a mass of 12 kg. The bench's control lamp draws 45 W. The stage total is the body's kinetic energy plus 14 J allowed for the trigger, and the bench performs 6 identical stages in a run. How much energy does a full run account for, in J?

A wind-tunnel logbook's closing entry takes the model's kinetic energy, subtracts 21 J for the sting heater, adds 19 J for the balance supply, and then adds a further 1 J for the datalogger. The model has a mass of 31000 g. Its speed in metres per second is taken from a calibration chart on which a plotted quantity equals 3 times the cube of the dial setting minus 1 times the square of the dial setting; the speed is the second-order rate of change of that plotted quantity with respect to the dial setting, evaluated at a dial setting of 2. The tunnel's contraction section is 4 m long. What is the logbook's closing entry, in J?

A go-kart club's season figure is 5 times the energy of a single race start, expressed in kilojoules. At a start, a kart and driver of combined mass 29 kg leave the line at a speed, in metres per second, found by taking a number x, adding 9, and then adding 16. The number x is the smaller of the two values for which x squared, minus 3 times x, plus 2, comes to exactly 0. The club's main straight is 180 m long. What is the club's season figure, in kJ?

A conveyor rig accelerates a pallet of mass 125 kg along a level track. The pallet's acceleration in metres per second squared equals the total that the drive's meter accumulates between the 1st and the 2nd second, where the meter's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 1 times t squared plus 3 times t. The rig's log takes the driving force, adds 9 N for the chain pretension, and then adds a further 30 N for the guide-roller drag. The rig's control cabinet is rated at 400 W. What figure does the rig's log give, in kN?

A bottling plant receives 278 caps of one type and 92 of another, and it packs them into identical boxes using the largest box size that divides both counts exactly. A test slug of mass 52000 g then moves along the runout at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to that box size. The plant runs 8 identical runouts at the same time, so the floor carries 8 times the energy of one slug, expressed in kilojoules. The plant's summary then adds 24 kJ for the air compressor. What does the plant's summary give, in kJ?

A tyre factory receives 242 valves of one kind and 165 of another, and it packs them in identical cartons using the largest carton size that divides both counts exactly. A test mass of 129000 g on the factory's shaker is then driven at an acceleration, in metres per second squared, numerically equal to that carton size. The engineering sheet takes the driving force in kilonewtons and subtracts 24 kN allowed for the shaker's own reaction frame. The factory runs 10 identical shakers, and the sheet reports 10 times the single-shaker figure. What does the engineering sheet report, in kN?

A theme-park operator's report is the park's energy figure plus 17 kJ charged to the ticket hall. The park's figure is 4 times a train's figure, since 4 identical trains run at once, and a train's figure is 8 times a single car's energy, since each train is made up of 8 cars. A loaded car has a mass of 27000 g. Its speed at the bottom of the drop, in metres per second, is the larger of the two values whose square, minus 11 times the value, plus 30, equals exactly 0. What does the operator's report give, in kJ?

A rail freight yard's annual figure is 4 times its monthly figure, and the monthly figure is 11 times the energy of a single train. A train is made up of 8 identical wagons, so it carries 8 times the energy of one wagon. Each wagon has a mass of 15 kg on the scale model used for the estimate. A wagon's speed, in metres per second, equals the total the model's meter accumulates between the 2nd and the 4th second of a run, where the meter's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 1 times t squared plus 3 times t. What is the yard's annual figure, in kJ?

A haulage test rig records a sled's speed in metres per second as 4 times the cube of the elapsed seconds plus 5 times the square of the elapsed seconds. The rig reads how fast that speed is changing at the instant 2 seconds in, then subtracts 26 to obtain the acceleration, in metres per second squared, that it applies to the load. The load has a mass of 159000 g, and the rig's cooling fan draws 120 W. Eleven identical rigs drive the same load in parallel, so the hall takes 11 times the single-rig force, and the log then subtracts 25 N for the frame's own reaction. What does the log record, in kN?

A machine shop's balance line reads the drive force in kilonewtons, adds 15 kN for the clamping ram, and then subtracts 16 kN for the counterweight. The driven slide has a mass of 41 kg. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is numerically equal to the largest whole number that divides both 65 and 315 exactly. The shop takes this balance reading before every production run. What does the balance line read, in kN?

A bobsleigh centre launches a test sled of mass 51000 g. The sled's launch speed in metres per second is twice the sum of the two track-gate readings, which are 2 and 13. The centre launches 11 sleds in a session, runs 7 sessions in a day, and operates 5 identical tracks at once. The centre's timing beam draws 60 W. How much energy do all the launches across the centre account for in a day, in kJ?

A depot's shift report gives the total force taken by 10 identical frames, each frame carrying 7 identical actuators pulling together. One actuator drives a slide of mass 71000 g. The slide's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is numerically equal to the largest whole number that divides both 190 and 177 exactly. The depot's inspection lamp is rated at 55 W. What total force does the shift report give, in kN?

A test track fires a sled whose speed, in metres per second, is 7 times the sum of the two throttle-stage settings, which read 2 and 9. The sled has a mass of 53 kg, and the track's marshalling light is rated at 75 W. The run sheet takes the sled's kinetic energy and adds 25 J for the release actuator. Expressed in kilojoules, the site's daily total then adds 11 kJ for the workshop supply and subtracts 30 kJ credited back by the regenerative brake. What is the site's daily total, in kJ?

A velodrome's test rig releases a dummy of mass 18 kg along the banking. The dummy's speed, in metres per second, is 7 times a number x, where x is the larger of the two values for which x squared, minus 9 times x, plus 20, equals exactly 0. The rig runs two identical lanes at once, so a session's total, in kilojoules, is twice the energy of one dummy. The session report then subtracts 6 kJ credited back by the regenerative catcher. What does the session report give, in kJ?

A luge training centre launches a sled of mass 48 kg. Its launch speed, in metres per second, is 6 more than a number x, where x is the smaller of the two values for which x squared, minus 14 times x, plus 48, equals exactly 0. The centre runs 7 launches in a heat and 9 heats in a day. The centre's start-gate lamp draws 55 W. The daily log then subtracts 3 J recovered by the catch net. What does the daily log record, in J?

A lift-testing hall reports the force taken by its 7 identical guide frames together. For one frame the reported force is the force driving the test car plus 30 N for the guide-shoe friction. The car has a mass of 115 kg, and the hall's shaft is 24 m deep. The car's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the smaller of the two values whose square, minus 9 times the value, plus 18, equals exactly 0. What force does the hall report for all 7 frames together, in kN?

A laboratory receives 301 washers of one size and 190 of another, and it groups them into identical trays using the largest tray size that divides both counts exactly. A bench cart of mass 24000 g then rolls at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to that tray size. The bench's energy sheet takes the cart's kinetic energy and adds 21 J drawn by the timer. It then subtracts 13 J recovered at the stop, and a further 26 J credited to the mains supply. What does the sheet total, in kJ?

A hangar's summary is 6 times a single bay's balance, because six identical bays operate together. A bay's balance is the force driving its tug, expressed in kilonewtons, less 19 kN allowed for the anchor chain. The tug pushes a load of mass 189 kg. That load's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is numerically equal to the largest whole number that divides both 93 and 14 exactly. What is the hangar's summary, in kN?

A rail-gun demonstration rig accelerates a slug of mass 16000 g. The slug's exit speed, in metres per second, equals the total that the rig's charge meter accumulates between the 0th and the 3rd second of a shot, where the meter's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 5 times t squared plus 6 times t. The rig's cooling pump is rated at 300 W. Each shot's booked energy is the slug's kinetic energy less 8 J absorbed by the muzzle brake, and the rig fires 6 shots in a demonstration. How much energy does a full demonstration account for, in kJ?

A drop-tower rig releases a carrier of mass 24 kg. The carrier's release speed in metres per second is read from a calibration chart on which a plotted quantity equals 3 times the cube of the dial setting plus 4 times the square of the dial setting; the speed is the second-order rate of change of that plotted quantity with respect to the dial setting, evaluated at a dial setting of 3. The tower's guide rail is 30 m long. Expressed in kilojoules, the site's energy sheet takes the carrier's kinetic energy, adds 27 kJ for the winch, adds 17 kJ for the compressor, and adds a further 29 kJ for the site cabin. What does the energy sheet total, in kJ?
